title: The Coherent State Projection Eigenvalue Theorem
authors: Peter D. Drummond, Margaret D. Reid
abstract: Recent papers have developed a cyclic symmetry projected extension for coherent state representations of bosonic Hilbert space. This extension can greatly reduce sampling errors in phase-space simulations of bosonic quantum systems that have symmetries. Here we prove an eigenvalue theorem for the continuum limit of the projected coherent states. Our intuitively appealing result is that in the continuum limit the projected coherent states are eigenstates of the symmetry generating operator. This result gives a differential identity in phase-space that includes the conserved eigenvalues. Detailed applications of these differential identities to obtaining improved Fokker-Planck and stochastic equations in many-body physics will be given elsewhere.
summary: This theoretical paper establishes an eigenvalue theorem for projected coherent states in bosonic systems possessing continuous symmetries. By analyzing the continuum limit of these projected states, the authors prove that they become eigenstates of the symmetry generator. This yields a crucial differential identity in phase-space, which can be used to improve numerical simulations of many-body quantum dynamics.
main_problem: The paper aims to prove an eigenvalue theorem for the continuum limit of projected coherent states when continuous symmetries are present in bosonic quantum systems.
main_result: In the continuum limit, the projected coherent states are shown to be eigenstates of the symmetry generating operator, yielding a differential identity in phase-space.
method: The authors utilize group theory to construct symmetry-projected coherent states and analyze their behavior in the limit of large projection orders ($M 	o \infty$).
